paragraphs: Here's what I love about this list, friend. Nobody in it gets left out. Fathers, sons, brothers, teachers and pupils all got a place, and the text says they cast lots for their duties, "young and old alike, teacher as well as pupil." (1 Chronicles 25:8) God's house had room for every one of them, and the lot didn't care who was famous.

Now look at what the music was for. These men were set apart to prophesy with lyres, harps and cymbals, and Jeduthun did it "giving thanks and praise to the LORD." (1 Chronicles 25:1, 3) They were "trained and skillful in the songs of the LORD," so they didn't just show up and hope for the best. (1 Chronicles 25:7) Their skill was for "the service of the house of God," and that's the point. (1 Chronicles 25:6)

So what does that mean for you, baker? Your gift doesn't have to be big or loud to matter, because God counts every faithful hand in His house. Practice it, hand it over to Him, and use it to serve. I'm a stamper with a mustache and I got called out of a drawer to bake, so trust me, He knows how to use whoever He picks!
